status_summary: No USDA policy limiting permanent easements was found: an NRCS Wetland Reserve Easements program page for the second FY2026 funding round (applications due 2026-05-29) still offers permanent easements alongside 30-year easements, and the FY2027 NRCS budget notes say Public Law 119-21 extended Agricultural Conservation Easement Program funding through 2031 without proposing any limit. S. 1495 (introduced 2025-04-10) would, in section 2(k), bar the NRCS Chief from acquiring any permanent easement, which matches the legislative part of the recommendation; no committee action or Administration endorsement was found. The House farm bill proposal, as summarized by an Oregon State University post, raises the federal cost share for agricultural land easements and creates a forest easement program, with no change to easement duration seen. H.R. 2773 (2025-04-09) would cap Interior Department easements at 30 years and does not cover USDA.

timeline.event: H.R. 2773, the Landowner Easement Rights Act, was introduced; it would limit new Interior Department conservation easements to 30 years and does not mention USDA.
S. 1495 was introduced; its section 2(k) would prohibit the NRCS Chief from acquiring any permanent easement.
An NRCS Wetland Reserve Easements program page listed permanent and 30-year easements as current enrollment options, with applications due 2026-05-29 for second-round FY2026 funding.
An Oregon State University post described the House farm bill proposal as raising the maximum federal cost share for agricultural land easements and creating a Forest Conservation Easement Program.

title: Limit permanent conservation easements and ask Congress to bar new ones
uncertainties: The FY2027 NRCS notes name Public Law 119-21 directly (under a popular title) as extending ACEP funding through 2031 and rescinding Inflation Reduction Act ACEP funding; the notes carry no publication date, so the date given is approximate. The House farm bill's easement provisions were read from a university summary and part of a long CRS comparison; neither shows a change to permanent versus term easements, so the absence is not conclusive. The Rhode Island program page is one state example; national NRCS policy on easement duration was not read. The S. 1495 actions page on congress.gov could not be opened. H.R. 2773 is related only by theme because it covers Interior, not USDA. Related to c10-12 because S. 1495 contains both the wetland compliance reforms and the permanent easement ban.
